You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: every wrong submission costs 1 and every demo request costs 1. An
instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# task-f1d2ef5b: diagonal extension variant (unresolved)

This ID has a variant where a sparse diagonal line of one color is extended, but the test rule is not validated. Do not reuse old guesses as a solution.

## Demos observed

- Demo 1, 28x20, bg6: color7 at (1,8),(2,7),(3,6) continues down-left to left edge: (4,5) through (9,0). Separately color4 at (1,9),(2,10) continues down-right from the latter to right edge at (11,19).
- Demo 2, 13x15, bg9: color6 at (8,12),(9,11) extends to (10,10),(11,9),(12,8). Other seed colors 8,4,7 remain untouched.
- Demo 3, 28x9, bg3: color9 at (24,2),(25,1) extends up-right to (18,8), preserving other colors.
- Demo 4, 16x5, bg5: color9 at (4,3),(5,2) extends down-left to (6,1),(7,0).
- Demo 5, 8x25, bg2: color6 at (4,3),(5,4) extends down-right to (6,5),(7,6).

General pattern suggested: continue collinear same-color diagonal runs through background to an edge, but test failures prove this alone is insufficient; a selector/direction criterion remains unknown.

## Later recurrence instance: explicit negative and gated diagonal

A fresh test contained only a 2x2 block near the lower-left: (19,2)=1,(19,3)=7,(20,2)=1,(20,3)=4 on bg9. Three demos were requested. Demo 1 (27x8, bg1) had non-bg at r7 c6=5,c7=0; r8 c6=6,c7=2 and output was unchanged. Demo 2 (9x19,bg5) had r0 c10=0,c11=0 and r1 c10=1,c11=6; output unchanged. Demo 3 (9x15,bg3) had 9 at (6,10),(7,11), with unrelated markers (7,12)=7,(8,11)=6,(8,12)=5. Output extended only 9 down-right from (6,10) through (7,11), and up-left from (7,11) to (0,4); all other markers unchanged. On test, correct output was unchanged input. Thus do not extend merely because there is a diagonal pair or adjacent multicolor 2x2. These demos remain insufficient to infer selector; safest use targeted demonstrations. The solved test confirms preserving the whole grid is correct for that specific arrangement.

## New recurrence observations (same instance, 2026-09-29)

Seven demonstrations across the instance established highly selective line extension, not blanket diagonal extension. Exact output changes by demo:

1. Demo 1: bg7, 14x16. Added color6 down-right (slope +1,+1) from (7,8) through (13,14), preserving the seed at (7,8). Added color4 up-right from (10,11) through (4,15), preserving existing (8,10),(7,11),(6,12),(5,13). Added color9 down-right from (10,11) to (13,14), preserving seed. Added color8 down-left from (10,9) to (13,6), preserving existing (9,9),(10,8). This looks like extending selected diagonals to boundary, with lines tied to different seed pairs/structures.
2. Demo 2: bg9 29x8. Added color5 up-left from (16,2) to (14,0), and further (17,3),(18,3) were existing color5; no changes to these latter aligned possibilities. This is weakly directional/selector evidence.
3. Demo 3: bg5 18x6. Only added color9 at (17,0), continuing up-left from (16,1); no other lines.
4. Demo 4: bg4 6x6. No changes despite several possible diagonal markers (3,6,5,0).
5. Demo 5: bg5 11x12. Extended color9 up-right from (5,2) to (0,7); extended color3 down-right from (8,2) through (10,4). Other markers unchanged.
6. Demo 6: bg1 18x13. No changes despite adjacent different-colored marks.
7. Demo 7: bg4 19x21. Extended color2 up-right from (2,12) through (0,14) and down-left from (3,11) through (14,0); extended color8 down-left from (5,9) through (14,0); extended color5 down-right from (5,12) through (13,20). Others preserved.

Test input non-background: 8 at (2,14),(3,15); 7 at (2,17),(3,16); 5 at (4,15),(5,14); 3 at (4,16),(5,17). Eight submissions all wrong. Failed guesses were various blanket extensions of these candidate diagonal runs in either/both directions, combinations, or preserved markers. Do not repeat. The selector remains unknown; examples 4 and 6 are explicit negatives. Do not assume all two-point diagonal motifs extend; infer an underlying selection condition from richer fresh demos. Attempt cap 8 and demo cap 8 in this instance; 7 demos used.

## New recurrence instance: no-op despite tempting diagonal (2026-09-29)

Test was 20x20 bg2 with non-bg cells: (14,0)=7; (15,1)=7,(15,2)=3; (16,1)=4,(16,2)=5. First demo (19x11, bg4) had 0 at (7,5),(8,6),(9,6),(10,5), 6s at (7,8),(8,7), and 3 at (9,7). Output extended 0 along the down-left diagonal from (7,5) through (15,0), and 6 down-left from (7,8) through (10,5); 3 at (9,7) unchanged. Second demo (24x16, bg5) had 2x2 marker block at rows3-4 cols8-9, colors 3,6,9,7; output was entirely unchanged. Test's tempting 7 diagonal continuation from (14,0) via (15,1) toward lower-right was submitted twice (one to edge, then one more cell) and both were wrong. Final accepted output was exactly the unchanged test input. This is strong instance-specific evidence that no-op can be correct even when an apparent same-color diagonal pair exists; do not extrapolate demo 1's diagonal rule indiscriminately. Record complete demos and importantly note final no-op validation.

## Test and failures (do not reuse outputs)

Test 25x6, bg3, non-bg positions: (21,4)=4; (22,2)=9,(22,3)=4; (23,2)=1,(23,3)=9; (24,1)=1. Eight guesses were incorrect, including extensions of colors 4 or 9, nearby recoloring, alternate starts, and preserving input. No selector or correct output was established. # Continual-ARC evidence calibration

Apply alongside ARC solving skills when demos and submissions have costs.

## task-cf7ceb8b validated vertical-separator variant (2026-09-29)

Two demos in one fresh instance established a specific rule: a full-height separator column of 2 lies just left of an irregular rectangular field. Translate the field one column left, preserve its internal holes/shape, and recolor the full-height column immediately to the field's right to 8. Demo 1 used bg5, separator c8, color0 motif c2–4 shifted to c4–6 (an unusual two-column shift) and stripe c7; demo 2 used bg9, separator c8, color1 field c10–15 shifted to c9–14 and stripe c15. Test had separator c6 and color4 pattern r15–22,c8–14; shift to c7–13 and stripe c14=8. Accepted with 0 wrong. Treat as instance-specific current-demo evidence, not a universal task-ID rule; this ID has other variants.

## Evidence before transfer
1. Treat each new instance as fresh. A matching task ID or stored recurrence note is only a hypothesis prior, not proof that this instance shares the same rule.
2. Before transforming the test, check current demos against any prior rule cell by cell. Record exact input markers, changed output cells, preserved cells, directions/anchors, and output colors. Verify at least one predicted transformed coordinate and one important unchanged coordinate.
3. If the demo has not arrived, never submit solely because a historical note calls the task “validated.” Request a demo when competing interpretations could materially change the output and the cost is justified.
4. After a wrong submission, identify the precise assumption it disproved. Do not make another submission based on that same unverified assumption or a minor variant; request a demo if available and rebuild from observed deltas.
5. Use one action per turn and follow the evaluator's exact JSON protocol. For puzzle turns, the final line must be exactly one valid action object.

## Pitfalls
- Historical notes can be stale or refer to a different variant despite identical task IDs. Current demo evidence wins.
- An unrelated or non-informative tool call is not a substitute for analyzing changed cells.
- Separate rule uncertainty from serialization errors; verify dimensions and row widths independently.

## References
See `references/task-f1d2ef5b-calibration.md` for an instance-specific example of rejecting a recurrence prior when feedback contradicts its prediction.

# Interactive ARC evaluation discipline

Use when puzzles arrive in turns with costly demos/submissions and a required action schema.

## Procedure
1. Treat the latest feedback, grid, and budget as authoritative. Extract changed cells from every demo before forming a rule.
2. Maintain a concise hypothesis ledger: list at most a few candidate selection/transformation rules, the changed and unchanged evidence each explains, and a specific observation that would distinguish them.
3. Request another demo only when its likely contents could discriminate among live hypotheses and its cost is justified. More examples are not inherently informative. Near the demo cap, stop broad requests and make the best evidence-supported submission rather than spending all remaining budget without a prediction.
4. Do not overstate inference. A visible correlation (for example, one component sharing a color or shape with a marker) is not a validated selection rule unless it accounts for the other demos and negative examples.
5. Construct outputs by preserving all unsupported cells; validate dimensions, row lengths, cell values, and all intended edits.
6. Follow the interface literally: exactly one action JSON on the final line of each evaluation reply. Avoid explanatory prose or unrelated tool activity in that protocol.

## Pitfalls
- Do not keep requesting demos without stating what evidence they are expected to resolve.
- Do not submit a broad speculative transformation because the budget is running out; prefer the smallest evidence-supported change.
- Separate rule uncertainty from transcription uncertainty; use a reliable grid construction/validation method for the latter.

## Related guidance
Use `continual-arc-solving` for ARC rule inference and `continual-arc-demo-followthrough` for immediate handling of demo turns.

# ARC demo grounding

Use with an ARC-solving skill when a puzzle offers costly demonstrations and submissions.

## task-55b70234 recurrence: fill framed interiors and 3x3 centers (expanded validation)

This task family uses shape-specific interior recoloring. Do not apply one fill color indiscriminately to every hollow outline: identify frame geometry and the corresponding center/interior color from demos.

A prior solved instance (background 8) demonstrated hollow 5x5 frames with 3x3 interiors filled 7, and a separate 3x3 block with its center changed to 7. Another test was solved correctly by filling the 5x5 frame's 3x3 cavity 7 and replacing the missing center of a separate 3x3 color9 object with 7.

Expanded recurrence, additional current validated variant (one demo; test solved on third submission with two wrong attempts): background 3. Demo shows a 7x7 outline with interior 5x5 filled 7; a separate 3x3 outline with only center empty has its center changed to 7. Test contained (a) 4x4 outline color4 with 2x2 cavity -> fill 2; (b) 7x7 outline color1 with 5x5 cavity -> fill 7; (c) 3x3 color8 object missing center -> center becomes 7. These reinforce the cavity-size mapping: 2x2 ->2, 3x3/5x5 ->7, and isolated center hole in 3x3 ->7. Validate grid serialization strictly: prior first guess malformed due wrong row width; second structurally valid but wrong because it used 7 for 2x2 cavity. Correct output preserves all outlines/exterior and applies the corresponding interior fill.

Expanded recurrence, 3 demos, test solved after five wrong submissions:
- Demo 1: 10x10 bg4; 7x7 square frame of 6 at rows1–7, cols0–6, cavity rows2–6, cols1–5 -> 7. This is a 5x5 interior. Confirms the large framed cavity fill color 7.
- Demo 2: 30x18 bg8. Multiple objects: 7x7 frame of 9 at r2–8,c4–10, interior 5x5 ->7; 3x3 frame of 3 at r1–3,c13–15 with one missing center at r2,c14 ->7; 4x4 frame of 3 at r10–13,c11–14 with 2x2 interior r11–12,c12–13 ->2; 9x7 frame of 6 at r14–20,c2–8 with interior r15–19,c3–7 ->7; 3x3 frame of 1 at r16–18,c10–12 with missing center ->7; another 3x3 frame of 1 at r21–23,c10–12 center ->7; 3x3 frame of 9 at r26–28,c5–7 center ->7; 3x3 frame of 0 at r26–28,c10–12 center ->7. Note the 2x2 cavity specifically filled with 2; multiple frame/component types coexist.
- Demo 3: 15x22 bg8. 5x5 frame of 4 at r0–4,c0–4 interior 3x3 ->7; 4x4 frame of 3 at r1–4,c15–18, interior 2x2 ->2; 5x5 frame of 6 at r6–12,c5–9, interior 5x3 ->7; 6x6 frame of 9 at r7–12,c15–20, interior 4x4 ->2. Thus 3x3 or 5x3 cavities get 7; 2x2 and 4x4 cavities get 2, regardless of frame color. The 3x3 objects with only center empty are also filled 7.

Solved test input 15x20, background 3: a 5x5 frame of 5 at r3–7,c2–6 with 3x3 interior r4–6,c3–5 filled 7; a 3x3 object of 6 at r10–12,c3–5 with center (11,4) changed to 7; a 5x5 frame of 5 at r9–13,c10–14 with 3x3 interior r10–12,c11–13 filled 7; a 7x7 frame of 4 at r0–7,c8–15 with 5x5 interior r1–6,c9–14 filled 2. This last large cavity requires 2, not 7. Correct submission was reached on wrong attempt 6, after five failed guesses.

General inference strongly supported: cavity dimensions determine fill color, at least in observed shapes: 2x2 or 4x4 ->2; 3x3, 5x3, 5x5 ->7. A centered single-cell hole in a 3x3 object ->7. Preserve border and exterior. For future variants, request demos when cavity-size mapping uncertain; don't use one global color for all interiors. Verify exact frame bounds and cavity dimensions.
## task-55b70234: framed cavity fill colors (new demo evidence)

A fresh 11x21 test was solved after the first grid submission was structurally invalid, one demo, and a corrected submission. Demo (11x10, bg=0) shows three separate outlined objects:
- 4x4 color-3 frame at rows0-3, cols0-3; its 2x2 interior (r1-2,c1-2) is filled with 2.
- 4x4 color-6 frame at rows2-5, cols5-8; its 2x2 interior (r3-4,c6-7) is filled with 2.
- 3x3 color-1 frame at rows7-9, cols3-5; its 1x1 center (r8,c4) is filled with 7.
Thus for this instance, 2x2 square cavities receive 2; a single-cell center cavity in a 3x3 outline receives 7. Preserve frames and background/exterior.

Correct test transformation: preserve all four outlines. Fill the 2x2 interior of the 4x4 color-1 frame (rows1-2, cols9-10) with 2. Fill the 3x3 cavity of the 5x5 color-5 frame (rows5-7, cols15-17) with 7. Fill the 3x3 cavity of the 5x5 color-8 frame (rows6-8, cols6-8) with 7. The previously submitted first attempt was INVALID ARC GRID because one row had the wrong width, despite the intended fills; corrected output was accepted. Always machine-check every row length and total dimensions before submission.

## task-d795d9b6 recurrence: marker interval variant with explicit singleton negative evidence
A fresh variant had background 7 and marker 4. In its only demo, row 4 contained markers at columns 2, 3, and 9; output recolored columns 4–8 to 3, leaving the markers intact. This supports recoloring background cells strictly between consecutive markers on a row (there were no demonstrated vertical pairs). The test had background 2 and a single marker 4 at row 1, column 9; correct output is unchanged, since there is no consecutive marker pair. This was accepted. Do not assume singleton markers or simply uniform-looking lines should change. As with other task-d795d9b6 variants, ground from current demos; other recurrences have demonstrated additional row-and-column interval behavior or different rules.
